entries.title: fopen
entries.summary: Open a file as a stream (FILE *).
entries.description: Returns NULL on failure and sets `errno`. Streams are buffered: data may reach the file only when the buffer is full or you call `fclose` or `fflush`.

details.name: "w"
details.text: write; creates the file or empties it

details.name: "a"
details.text: append at the end; creates it if missing

details.name: "r+"
details.text: read and write; must exist; not emptied

details.name: "w+"
details.text: read and write; creates or empties

details.name: "a+"
details.text: read anywhere, write always at the end

mistakes: Using "w" when you meant to keep the old content.

entries.title: fclose
entries.description: Writes the buffered data, releases the stream and returns 0 (or `EOF` on error). Without it the last data may never reach the file.
mistakes: Forgetting to close a file you wrote to.

entries.title: fflush
entries.summary: Write the buffered output of a stream now.
entries.description: Useful before a prompt, before `fork`, or before switching to low-level calls on the same file. `fflush(stdout)` makes the prompt visible even without a newline.

entries.title: fread
entries.syntax: size_t fread(void *ptr, size_t size, size_t n, FILE *stream);
entries.description: Reads up to `n` items of `size` bytes and returns the number of ITEMS read. A short count means end of file or an error: tell them apart with `feof` and `ferror`. The bytes are stored exactly as in the file.
mistakes: Writing `sizeof buf` bytes at the end of the file instead of the `n` read.

entries.title: fwrite
entries.syntax: size_t fwrite(const void *ptr, size_t size, size_t n, FILE *stream);
entries.description: Writes `n` items of `size` bytes and returns the number of items written; less than `n` means an error.
mistakes: Swapping `size` and `n` (the return value then counts differently).

entries.title: fseek
entries.summary: Move the position in a stream.
entries.syntax: int fseek(FILE *stream, long offset, int whence);
entries.description: Returns 0 on success. `whence` is the origin of the offset.

details.name: SEEK_SET
details.text: from the start of the file

details.name: SEEK_END
details.text: from the end of the file (the offset is usually negative or 0)

entries.title: ftell
entries.description: Returns the offset in bytes from the start, or -1 on error. After `fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END)` it is the file size.

entries.title: rewind
entries.summary: Go back to the start of a stream.
entries.description: Equivalent to `fseek(stream, 0, SEEK_SET)` and clears the error and end-of-file flags.

entries.title: fgetpos
entries.summary: Save the position of a stream (as an opaque fpos_t).
entries.description: Stores the current position in `*pos`; restore it later with `fsetpos`. Works for positions that do not fit in a long.

entries.title: fsetpos
entries.summary: Restore a position saved with fgetpos.

entries.title: feof
entries.summary: Has the end of the file been reached (by a previous read)?
entries.description: True only AFTER a read hit the end of the file, so `while (!feof(f))` runs once too often. Test the return value of the read function instead; use `feof` to find out why a read stopped.
entries.example:
if (fgets(buf, sizeof buf, f) == NULL && feof(f))
    puts("end of file");

entries.title: ferror
entries.summary: Did a read or write on the stream fail?
entries.description: Non-zero if the error flag is set. Together with `feof` it explains why a read function returned fewer items than asked.

entries.title: fdopen
entries.summary: Wrap an open file descriptor in a stream.
entries.description: Lets you use stdio functions on a descriptor from `open`, `dup2` or a pipe. Closing the stream closes the descriptor.

entries.title: fileno
entries.summary: The file descriptor of a stream.
entries.description: Returns the integer descriptor (stdin is 0, stdout 1, stderr 2). Useful with `dup2` and `fstat`.

entries.title: rename
entries.description: Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. If `new` exists it is replaced.
